title: INDEC: Poverty Rate Jumps to 32.3% in First Half of 2026, Reversing Milei-Era Decline
detail: INDEC reported the poverty rate rose to 32.3% in the first half of 2026, up 4.1 points from 28.2% in the second half of 2025, as incomes failed to keep pace with the cost of living — average per-capita household income rose 11.5% while the basic basket used to set the poverty line rose nearly 20%. Roughly 9.7 million people across 31 surveyed urban areas live below the poverty line, including 2.25 million in extreme poverty; nearly 45% of Argentines aged 14 and under are classified as poor. A September AtlasIntel survey found the deterioration concentrated among lower-income voters — disapproval among respondents earning up to roughly $650/month climbed to nearly 70% (from 57% a year earlier), with approval in that bracket falling below 30%. Nationally, AtlasIntel put Milei's approval at 38.1% against 58% disapproval, one year before his 2027 reelection bid.

media.caption: Argentina's poverty rate rises above 30% under President Milei, reversing recent decline

title: Milei Rejects Recession Talk, Says He's 'Calm' About 2027 Reelection
detail: Speaking at an Economic Club of New York event in an interview with Bloomberg Editor-in-Chief John Micklethwait, President Milei downplayed concerns over Argentina's stalling economy — including the Q2 2026 GDP contraction and rising poverty and unemployment — saying 'we don't see any problem with growth' and that he remains 'very calm' about his prospects for reelection in 2027. Milei projected that, if reelected, 2028 would be 'the best year of Argentine economic history' in both financial and real-economy terms. The remarks came the same day INDEC data showed poverty climbing to 32.3%.

media.caption: Milei rejects recession talk, says he's 'calm' about re-election
